**Day 1 Itinerary: Beijing to Shanghai **

### 06:35–08:50 | Travel to Shanghai  
Start your journey with a **flight** on **CA3202** from **Beijing** to **Shanghai**. Depart at 06:35 and arrive at 08:50, ensuring a punctual and comfortable trip.  
- **Ticket Price**: ¥520  

---

### 09:30–10:00 | Check-in at Yaduo Hotel  
After arriving in Shanghai, check in at **Yaduo Hotel**, an **Upscale hotel** with a 4.5/5 rating. Enjoy a comfortable stay at an average price of ¥546 per night. Guests have praised the hotel for its **excellent environment** (9.0/10) and **top-notch service** (9.0/10).  
- **Average Price Per Night**: ¥546  

---

### 10:30–13:00 | Oriental Pearl Tower  
Visit the iconic **Oriental Pearl Tower**, a 468-meter-tall landmark offering stunning 360-degree views of Shanghai. Explore the observation decks, suspended sightseeing corridor, and rotating restaurant at 267 meters. Perfect for capturing panoramic views of the Huangpu River and Lujiazui skyline.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–21:00 (Admission ends at 20:30)  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥195  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-3 hours  

---

### 14:00–16:00 | Nanjing Road Pedestrian Street  
Stroll along **Nanjing Road Pedestrian Street**, one of China’s top ten famous pedestrian streets. Enjoy shopping, urban sculptures, and the nostalgic charm of old Shanghai with clanging trams. A shopper’s paradise and a great spot for people-watching.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1-3 hours  

---

### 17:00–18:30 | The Bund  
End your day with a leisurely walk along **The Bund**, Shanghai’s most iconic waterfront area. Admire the historic foreign buildings on one side and the modern skyscrapers of Lujiazui on the other. Perfect for capturing the city’s charm and romance, especially as the neon lights illuminate the Huangpu River.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1-3 hours  

---

### 19:00–20:00 | Dinner at laiyifen  
Enjoy dinner at **laiyifen**, a hot pot restaurant offering a cozy dining experience. While the ratings are modest (3.5/5), it’s a convenient spot to unwind after a day of exploration.  
- **Average Price**: ¥181.5  
- **Rating**: 3.5/5

**Day 2 Itinerary**

### 09:30–13:00 | China National Maritime Museum  
Kick off your day at the **China National Maritime Museum**, the largest and highest-ranking maritime museum in China. Explore six main exhibition halls, including Maritime History, Ships, and Military Maritime, along with special areas like Fishing Vessels and Maritime Sports. Don’t miss the Planetarium, 4D Cinema, and Children's Activity Center for an immersive experience.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:30–16:00 (last admission at 15:30)  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥27  
- **Recommended Duration**: 3-4 hours  

### 13:00–14:00 | Lunch at Dishui Lake No. 1 Kitchen  
Head to **Dishui Lake No. 1 Kitchen** for a seafood lunch. This restaurant offers fresh and flavorful dishes in a relaxed setting, perfect for refueling after your museum visit.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Seafood  
- **Average Cost**: ¥124.5  

### 14:30–18:00 | Shanghai Wild Animal Park  
Spend the afternoon at **Shanghai Wild Animal Park**, a sprawling 153-hectare park home to over 200 species of rare animals. Get up close with giant pandas, giraffes, zebras, and more, and enjoy special animal behavior demonstrations.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–16:30 (last admission at 15:30)  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥165  
- **Recommended Duration**: 0.5-1 day  

### 18:30–19:30 | Dinner at Tang Ji Chuan Cai  
End your day with a delightful dinner at **Tang Ji Chuan Cai**, known for its authentic Jiangsu and Zhejiang cuisine. Enjoy a mix of traditional flavors in a warm and inviting atmosphere.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Jiangsu and Zhejiang Cuisine  
- **Average Cost**: ¥159

**Day 3 Itinerary**

### 09:00–21:30 | Shanghai Disney Resort  
Kick off your day at **Shanghai Disney Resort**, the first Disney theme park in mainland China. Explore seven enchanting themed areas, including Mickey Avenue, Fantasyland, and Tomorrowland. Don’t miss the iconic **Fantasy Fairy Tale Castle**, the largest Disney castle in the world, and enjoy interactive experiences with beloved Disney characters.  
- **Opening Hours**: 08:30–21:30  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥399  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1-2 days  

### 12:00–13:00 | Lunch at Yifeng Hall Ramen  
Take a break for lunch at **Yifeng Hall Ramen**, a cozy spot offering authentic Japanese ramen. Relish the rich flavors of their signature dishes in a relaxed atmosphere.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Japanese  
- **Average Cost**: ¥124.5  

### 18:00–19:00 | Dinner at Nanxiaoguan  
End your day with a delightful dinner at **Nanxiaoguan**, known for its refined Jiangsu and Zhejiang cuisine. Enjoy a mix of traditional flavors and modern presentations in an elegant setting.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Jiangsu and Zhejiang  
- **Average Cost**: ¥130.5

**Day 4 Itinerary**

### 09:00–12:00 | Shanghai Natural History Museum  
Kick off your day at the **Shanghai Natural History Museum**, one of China’s largest museums of its kind. Explore five floors of exhibits showcasing tens of thousands of specimens, including the impressive 26-meter-long Mamenxi Dragon skeleton. The Discovery Center is a hit with kids, offering interactive activities.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–17:00 (Admission ends at 16:00)  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥30  
- **Recommended Duration**: 0.5-1 day  

---

### 12:00–13:00 | Lunch at Black Forest Food  
Enjoy a flavorful lunch at **Black Forest Food**, known for its hot pot dishes. The cozy ambiance and hearty meals make it a great spot to refuel.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Hot Pot  
- **Average Cost**: ¥195  

---

### 13:00–15:00 | Wukang Road  
Stroll along **Wukang Road**, a historic street lined with 37 historical buildings, including the iconic Wukang Building. Admire the European-style architecture and lush greenery while learning about the area’s rich cultural heritage.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1-2 hours

After arriving in Guangzhou, check in at **Chateau Star River Hotel**, a **Luxury hotel** with a 5.0/5 rating. Enjoy a comfortable stay at an average price of ¥994 per night. Guests have praised the hotel for its **excellent service** (9.0/10) and **pleasant environment** (8.4/10).  
- **Average Price Per Night**: ¥994  

---

Head to **Patus Grill** for a Western-style lunch. This restaurant offers a variety of dishes with a price of ¥744. While the ratings are modest (3.5/5 overall), it’s a convenient option for a midday meal.  
- **Price**: ¥744  
- **Rating**: 3.5/5  

---

### 14:00–17:00 | Explore Chimelong Birds Park  
Visit **Chimelong Birds Park**, a large-scale natural ecological wetland park home to tens of thousands of rare birds. Enjoy intimate encounters with flamingos, red-crowned cranes, and more. The park is divided into themed areas like Crocodile Dancing and Swan Bay, offering interactive experiences.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:30–18:00  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥100  
- **Recommended Duration**: 3-5 hours  

---

Savor a spicy Sichuan hotpot dinner at **Hongyunlou Sichuan Hotpot**. This restaurant offers a flavorful experience at a reasonable price of ¥207. While the ratings are modest (3.5/5), it’s a great spot for hotpot lovers.  
- **Price**: ¥207  
- **Rating**: 3.5/5  

---

### 19:30–21:30 | Guangzhou Chimelong International Circus  
End your day with a spectacular performance at **Guangzhou Chimelong International Circus**. Featuring over 300 circus elites and 500 rare animals, this show is staged on the world’s largest live forest stage. The performance includes animal acts, acrobatics, and a magical float parade.  
- **Opening Hours**: 17:00–21:00  
- **Ticket Price**: ¥350  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2 hours

Kick off your day at **Chimelong Paradise**, a thrilling theme park offering a mix of adrenaline-pumping rides, vibrant performances, and family-friendly attractions. Explore six themed areas, including Jungle Adventure and Scream Zone, and enjoy the grand "Joyful and Colorful Parade" with its massive floats and interactive stages. Don’t miss the Circus Town and Cookie Factory for a whimsical experience.  
- **Opening Hours**: 10:00–18:00  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥250  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1 day  

---

- **Cuisine Type**: Japanese  
- **Average Cost**: ¥501  

---

- **Cuisine Type**: Guangdong  
- **Average Cost**: ¥223.5

Spend your final day exploring **Chimelong Safari Park**, Asia's largest wildlife park, featuring over 500 rare animal species, including China's iconic giant pandas. Enjoy thrilling performances like the white tiger show and the humorous elephant performances. Take a small train ride through the jungles and grasslands for an immersive wildlife experience.

- **Recommended Duration**: 1 day  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:30–18:00

**Day 1 Itinerary: Nanjing to Shenzhen **

### 07:00–09:20 | Travel to Shenzhen

- **Average Price Per Night**: ¥372

Explore the **Shenzhen Museum of Contemporary Art and Urban Planning**, a futuristic architectural marvel featuring unique exhibitions and a stunning design. The museum is known for its innovative displays and the iconic "Cloud Sculpture" connecting the two pavilions.

Stroll through **East Gate Shopping Mall**, one of Shenzhen's oldest and most vibrant commercial streets. With thousands of shops and a lively atmosphere, it’s a great place to experience local culture and shop for souvenirs.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7

**Day 2 Itinerary**

Kick off your day at **Window of the World**, a man-made theme park that showcases miniature replicas of global wonders, historical sites, and cultural performances. Don’t miss the evening shows if you stay late!

- **Average Cost**: ¥166.5

Immerse yourself in art at **He Xiangning Art Museum**, the first national art museum named after an individual in China. The museum’s serene architecture and tranquil atmosphere make it a perfect escape.

Continue your artistic journey at **Hua Art Museum**, a design-focused space showcasing contemporary art and innovative design. - **Opening Hours**: 10:00–17:30 (Admission ends at 17:00)

- **Recommended Duration**: 1-2 hours

**Day 1 Itinerary: Shenzhen to Shanghai **

### 06:40–08:55 | Travel to Shanghai  
Start your journey with a **flight** on **CZ3568** from **Shenzhen** to **Shanghai**. Depart at 06:40 and arrive at 08:55, ensuring a punctual and comfortable trip.  
- **Ticket Price**: ¥660  

---

### 09:30–10:00 | Check-in at Aibo Fashion Hotel  
After arriving in Shanghai, check in at **Aibo Fashion Hotel**, an **Economy hotel** with a 4.0/5 rating. Enjoy a comfortable stay at an average price of ¥282 per night. Guests have praised the hotel for its **pleasant environment** (7.8/10) and **good service** (7.8/10).  
- **Average Price Per Night**: ¥282  

---

### 12:00–13:00 | Lunch at Qingxiangyuan Beef Noodles  
Head to **Qingxiangyuan Beef Noodles** for a quick and satisfying lunch. This fast-food spot offers hearty beef noodles at an affordable price of ¥42. While the ambiance is simple, the food is a solid choice for a midday meal.  
- **Price**: ¥42  
- **Rating**: 3.5/5  

---

### 15:00–17:00 | Explore The Bund  
Stroll along **The Bund**, one of Shanghai’s most iconic attractions. Enjoy the stunning views of the Huangpu River, historic architecture, and the modern skyline of Lujiazui. Perfect for a leisurely walk and photo opportunities.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1-3 hours  

---

### 18:00–19:00 | Dinner at Muslim Western Cowboy Noodle Restaurant  
For dinner, visit **Muslim Western Cowboy Noodle Restaurant**, a casual spot offering flavorful noodle dishes at a budget-friendly price of ¥27. It’s a great place to experience local snacks.  
- **Price**: ¥27  
- **Rating**: 3.5/5  

---

### 19:00–21:00 | Huangpu River Cruise (Shiliupu Pier)  
End your day with a scenic **Huangpu River Cruise** from **Shiliupu Pier**. Marvel at the illuminated skyline of Shanghai, including landmarks like the Oriental Pearl Tower and Lujiazui Financial District. A perfect way to experience the city’s vibrant nightlife.  
- **Opening Hours**: 11:00–22:00  
- **Ticket Price**: ¥90  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1-2 hours

**Day 2 Itinerary**

### 09:00–16:30 | Shanghai Wild Animal Park  
Kick off your day at **Shanghai Wild Animal Park**, a sprawling 153-hectare sanctuary that offers close encounters with over 200 species of rare animals, including giant pandas, giraffes, and cheetahs. Explore the park’s diverse zones, enjoy animal behavior demonstrations, and immerse yourself in a blend of education and entertainment.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–16:30 (last admission at 15:30)  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥165  
- **Recommended Duration**: 0.5–1 day  

---

### 12:00–13:00 | Lunch at Xi Yongji  
Refuel with a quick and affordable lunch at **Xi Yongji**, a casual spot offering a variety of local snacks. Perfect for a light meal, this eatery provides a simple yet satisfying dining experience.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Snacks  
- **Average Cost**: ¥24  

---

### 18:00–19:00 | Dinner at Riyueban Noodle Restaurant  
End your day with a comforting meal at **Riyueban Noodle Restaurant**, known for its flavorful noodle dishes. The cozy ambiance and friendly service make it a great spot to unwind after a day of exploration.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Snacks  
- **Average Cost**: ¥28.5

**Day 3 Itinerary**

### 09:00–12:00 | Shanghai Ocean Aquarium  
Begin your day at **Shanghai Ocean Aquarium**, a fascinating underwater world spread across three floors. Explore themed exhibition areas like the China Exhibition Area and the Americas Exhibition Area, showcasing a diverse range of marine species. Don’t miss the world’s only observation tunnel featuring the Amazon rainforest. Perfect for families, this aquarium offers a unique chance to stroll through an underwater tunnel and observe marine life up close.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–18:00 (last entry at 17:30)  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥155  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1-3 hours  

---

### 12:00–13:00 | Lunch at Shandong Dumplings  
For lunch, head to **Shandong Dumplings**, a casual spot specializing in wontons and dumplings. Enjoy freshly made dumplings in a simple, no-frills setting.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Wontons and Dumplings  
- **Average Cost**: ¥22.5  

---

### 14:00–16:00 | Wukang Road  
Spend the afternoon exploring **Wukang Road**, a historic street lined with 37 historical buildings, including 14 well-preserved ones. Known as the “Celebrity Road,” it features European-style architecture, lush greenery, and landmarks like the Wukang Building, designed by renowned architect Hudec. Stroll past former residences of famous figures like Ba Jin and Huang Xing, and soak in the charm of this century-old road.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1-2 hours  

---

### 16:00–18:00 | Anfu Road  
Continue your cultural exploration at **Anfu Road**, a hub for Shanghai’s literary and artistic scene. This charming street is dotted with coffee shops, wine cellars, and art spaces. Take a leisurely walk, enjoy the quiet ambiance, and perhaps stop for a coffee at one of the quaint cafes.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1-2 hours  

---

### 18:00–19:00 | Dinner at laoshengchang baozi  
End your day with a quick and satisfying meal at **laoshengchang baozi**, a fast-food spot known for its delicious baozi (steamed buns). Enjoy these local favorites in a simple, casual setting.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Fast Food  
- **Average Cost**: ¥31.5

**Itinerary for the Last Day of the Trip**

### 10:00–12:00 | Visit City God Temple Tourist Area  
Begin your final day with a visit to the **City God Temple Tourist Area**, a must-see attraction in Shanghai that offers a glimpse into its rich history, culture, and customs. Wander through the Old Chenghuang Temple and Yuyuan Garden, capturing stunning night views if you're there as dusk falls.  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free (Note: Some areas require tickets)  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-3 hours  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  

### 12:00–13:00 | Lunch at Laotianmu Stewed Meat Expert  
Savor authentic Northeastern cuisine at **Laotianmu stewed meat expert**. Enjoy their signature dishes in a cozy setting, rated reasonably well for food quality, ambiance, and service.  
- **Price per Person**: ¥33  
- **Rating**: 3.5/5

**Day 1 Itinerary: Beijing to Guangzhou **

### 06:30–09:50 | Travel to Guangzhou  
Start your journey with a **flight** on **CZ3166** from **Beijing** to **Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport**. Depart at 06:30 and arrive at 09:50, ensuring a punctual and comfortable trip.  
- **Ticket Price**: ¥830  

---

### 10:30–11:00 | Check-in at Guangzhou Building  
After arriving in Guangzhou, check in at **Guangzhou Building**, an **Upscale hotel** with a **5.0/5 rating**. Enjoy a luxurious stay at an average price of ¥525 per night. Guests have praised the hotel for its **excellent environment** (9.0/10) and **top-notch service** (9.0/10).  
- **Average Price Per Night**: ¥525  

---

### 14:00–16:00 | Huacheng Square  
Explore **Huacheng Square**, the new central axis square of Guangzhou. Admire the artificial landscape lakes, large fountains, and vibrant lighting squares. The underground commercial area, Huachenghui, offers a variety of dining options. At night, the square is beautifully lit, making it a perfect spot for nighttime sightseeing.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-3 hours  

---

### 16:30–18:30 | Canton Tower  
Visit the iconic **Canton Tower**, a 600-meter-tall landmark known for its dazzling night views. Enjoy attractions like the Ferris wheel, Pearl River photography viewing platform, and Spider-Man walkway. The tower lights up at night, offering a stunning visual experience.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:30–22:30 (Admission ends at 22:00)  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥145  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-3 hours  

---

### 19:00–20:00 | Dinner at Sheng 'an Hotel  
Conclude your day with dinner at **Sheng 'an Hotel**, known for its **Guangdong cuisine**. Enjoy a meal at an average price of ¥106.5. While the restaurant has a modest rating (3.5/5), it offers a convenient dining option near your hotel.  
- **Average Price**: ¥106.5  
- **Rating**: 3.5/5  

---

**Day 2 Itinerary**

### 09:00–11:00 | Shamian  
Kick off your day with a stroll through **Shamian**, a historic neighborhood that feels like a slice of Europe in Guangzhou. Known for its European-style architecture, this former British and French concession is perfect for photography, with landmarks like the Catholic Church of Our Lady of Lude and the Customs House. The area is dotted with charming cafes, bars, and restaurants, making it a delightful place to explore.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1-3 hours  

---

### 11:00–12:00 | Chen Clan Ancestral Hall  
Next, visit the **Chen Clan Ancestral Hall**, a stunning example of late Qing Dynasty architecture. This ancestral hall is renowned for its intricate wood, stone, and brick carvings, as well as its beautifully preserved structure. Wander through its interconnected courtyards and admire the craftsmanship that makes this a must-see cultural gem.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–17:30 (last entry at 17:00)  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 0.5-2 hours  

---

### 12:00–13:00 | Lunch at Niu Chuangwei Chaoshan Beef Hotpot  
For lunch, indulge in **Chaoshan Beef Hotpot** at **Niu Chuangwei Chaoshan Beef Hotpot**. This restaurant offers a flavorful hotpot experience with tender beef slices and a variety of dipping sauces. The casual ambiance makes it a great spot to refuel after a morning of sightseeing.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Hot Pot  
- **Average Cost**: ¥112.5 per person  

---

### 13:15–14:00 | Shishi Sacred Heart Cathedral  
After lunch, head to the **Shishi Sacred Heart Cathedral**, one of the largest Gothic-style churches in China. Admire its towering spires and intricate stonework, and step inside to experience the serene atmosphere. Note that photography is prohibited inside during non-Mass hours.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–11:00, 15:00–17:00  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 15-45 minutes  

---

### 14:00–16:00 | Yuexiu Park  
Spend the afternoon at **Yuexiu Park**, Guangzhou’s largest park, known for its lush greenery and historical landmarks. Highlights include the iconic Five Rams Statue, the ancient city walls, and the Sun Yat-sen Monument. The park’s scenic lakes and walking paths make it a relaxing escape in the heart of the city.  
- **Opening Hours**: 06:00–22:00  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-4 hours  

---

### 16:00–19:00 | Canton Orchid Garden  
Conclude your afternoon at the **Canton Orchid Garden**, a tranquil botanical garden specializing in orchids. With over 200 varieties and nearly 10,000 pots of orchids, the garden is a feast for the senses. Enjoy the peaceful ambiance, take photos of the vibrant blooms, and relax in one of the elegant tea rooms.  
- **Opening Hours**: 08:00–18:00  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥8  
- **Recommended Duration**: 3 hours  

---

### 19:00–20:00 | Dinner at Taoyuan Food Shop  
For dinner, try **Hunan Cuisine** at **Taoyuan Food Shop**. Known for its bold and spicy flavors, this restaurant offers a variety of dishes that showcase the best of Hunan’s culinary traditions. The cozy yet stylish setting makes it a great place to unwind after a busy day.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Hunan Cuisine  
- **Average Cost**: ¥102 per person  

---

### 20:00–22:00 | Pearl River Night Cruise  
End your day with a **Pearl River Night Cruise**, where you can admire Guangzhou’s dazzling skyline illuminated at night. The cruise passes iconic landmarks like the Canton Tower and Haixinsha Island, offering a magical perspective of the city.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–22:30  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥98  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1-2 hours

**Day 3 Itinerary**

### 09:00–10:00 | Guangzhou Cultural Center (New Building)  
Begin your day at the **Guangzhou Cultural Center (New Building)**, a stunning architectural marvel that blends traditional Lingnan garden aesthetics with modern design. Explore themed gardens like Hanmo Garden, Quyi Garden, and Guangfu Garden, which recreate the charm of a Lingnan water town. This cultural hub is a perfect introduction to Guangzhou’s rich heritage and natural beauty.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–17:30 (Admission ends at 16:30)  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1-2 hours  

---

### 12:00–13:00 | Lunch at Xiangju Xiahuang  
For lunch, head to **Xiangju Xiahuang**, a popular spot for **crayfish** dishes. Enjoy the bold flavors of this local specialty in a casual, laid-back setting. The restaurant offers a vibrant atmosphere, perfect for a midday break.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Crayfish  
- **Average Cost**: ¥184.5 per person  

---

### 13:00–15:00 | The Memorial Hall of the Former Site of Huangpu Military Academy  
Next, visit **The Memorial Hall of the Former Site of Huangpu Military Academy**, a historic site that played a pivotal role in modern Chinese military history. Explore the Republic of China-era architecture, including the school headquarters and Sun Yat-sen’s former residence. Guided tours are available at specific times, offering deeper insights into this iconic landmark.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–17:00 (Admission ends at 16:30)  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-4 hours  

---

### 15:00–18:00 | Lingnan Impression Garden  
Spend the afternoon at **Lingnan Impression Garden**, a cultural destination that showcases traditional Lingnan architecture and folk customs. Wander through charming streets and alleys, and immerse yourself in the nostalgic charm of ancient Lingnan culture. The garden also offers performances and dining options, making it a perfect spot for relaxation and exploration.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:30–18:00 (Admission ends at 17:00)  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥49  
- **Recommended Duration**: 3-5 hours  

---

### 18:00–19:00 | Dinner at Aloft Hotel Jujule Restaurant  
End your day with a delightful dinner at **Aloft Hotel Jujule Restaurant**, known for its **buffet** offerings. Enjoy a variety of dishes in a modern, stylish setting, perfect for unwinding after a day of sightseeing.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Buffet  
- **Average Cost**: ¥184.5 per person

**Itinerary for the Last Day of the Trip**

### 09:00–12:00 | Visit Baiyun Mountain  
Kick off your final day with a visit to **Baiyun Mountain**, a renowned natural landmark known as the "First Beauty of Yangcheng." Explore its 30+ peaks, enjoy panoramic views of Guangzhou, and marvel at the swirling clouds that give the mountain its name. - **Recommended Duration**: 0.5–1 day

### 12:30–13:30 | Lunch at Oriental Resort  
Refuel with a delicious meal at **Oriental Resort**, a restaurant specializing in authentic Guangdong cuisine. Enjoy the cozy ambiance and savor dishes that highlight the region’s culinary traditions.  
- **Price**: ¥126 per person  
- **Rating**: 3.5/5  

### 14:00–16:00 | Explore Yuntai Garden  
Next, head to **Yuntai Garden**, the largest western-style garden in China. Wander through its beautifully landscaped areas, including the Rose Garden, Glass Greenhouse, and Sun Square. The garden’s blend of Eastern and Western architectural styles makes it a unique and tranquil retreat.  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥10  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1–2 hours  
- **Opening Hours**: 08:00–18:00

Conclude your sightseeing with a visit to the **Beijing Road Cultural Tourism Zone**, a historic pedestrian street that blends ancient charm with modern vibrancy. Walk along the cobblestone road, explore the millennium-old ruins under glass, and soak in the bustling atmosphere of this commercial hub.  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2–3 hours  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  

### 18:30 | Hotel Check-Out  
Check out from your hotel and store your luggage if needed. Ensure you have all your belongings before heading to the airport.  

### 20:00–23:10 | Flight to Beijing  
End your trip with a **flight** on **CZ3161** from **Guangzhou** to **Beijing**. Depart at 20:00 and arrive at 23:10, ensuring a smooth and timely journey back home.

**Day 1 Itinerary: Shenzhen to Xi'an **

### 06:45–09:25 | Travel to Xi'an  
Start your journey with a **flight** on **9C8753** from **Shenzhen** to **Xi'an Xianyang International Airport**. Depart at 06:45 and arrive at 09:25, ensuring a punctual and comfortable trip.  
- **Ticket Price**: ¥720  

---

### 10:00–10:30 | Check-in at Long March Mirasot Hotel  
After arriving in Xi'an, check in at **Long March Mirasot Hotel**, an **Upscale hotel** with a **4.5/5 rating**. Enjoy a comfortable stay at an average price of ¥424 per night. Guests have praised the hotel for its **excellent service** (9.0/10) and **pleasant environment** (8.0/10).  
- **Average Price Per Night**: ¥424  

---

### 12:00–13:00 | Lunch at Zhangbaba Chuanchuan Hot Pot  
Savor authentic **Hot Pot** at **Zhangbaba Chuanchuan Hot Pot**, a local favorite known for its flavorful broths and fresh ingredients. The restaurant offers a cozy atmosphere with a **7.6/10 environment rating** and friendly service (7.8/10).  
- **Average Price Per Person**: ¥105  

---

### 15:00–16:00 | Xi'An City Tour  
Hop on the **Xi'An City Tour** bus for a scenic ride through the city. This tour highlights the **Tang Culture** and offers a unique perspective of Xi'an's urban landscape. The bus stops at various sightseeing stations, allowing you to explore at your own pace.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–20:20  
- **Ticket Price**: ¥49.9  
- **Recommended Duration**: 0.5–1 hour  

---

### 18:00–19:00 | Dinner at Qingduli · Si Chu  
Indulge in **Japanese Cuisine** at **Qingduli · Si Chu**, a highly-rated restaurant with a serene ambiance (8.7/10 environment rating). The menu features exquisite dishes, perfect for a relaxing evening meal.  
- **Average Price Per Person**: ¥192  

---

### 19:00–21:00 | Explore Muslim Quarter  
Stroll through the vibrant **Muslim Quarter**, a bustling neighborhood filled with street food vendors and cultural landmarks. Sample local delicacies like **meat sandwiches** and **steamed buns** while soaking in the lively atmosphere.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2–3 hours  

---

### 21:00–22:00 | Nighttime Visit to Xi'an Bell Tower  
End your day with a visit to the iconic **Xi'an Bell Tower**, beautifully illuminated at night. This historical landmark offers stunning views of the city and a glimpse into Xi'an's rich heritage.  
- **Opening Hours**: 08:30–18:00 (Note: Nighttime viewing is from the exterior only)  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥30  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1–2 hours

**Day 2 Itinerary**

### 09:00–12:00 | Xi'an Museum  
Begin your day at **Xi'an Museum**, a comprehensive exhibition area that integrates museums, historical sites, and urban gardens. Explore nearly 130,000 historical relics, including precious cultural items from the Zhou, Qin, Han, and Tang dynasties. Don’t miss the "Ancient Capital Xi'an" exhibition and the detailed model of Xi'an's city walls, showcasing the evolution of the ancient capitals.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–17:30 (Admission ends at 16:30)  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-3 hours  

---

### 12:00–13:00 | Lunch at Cantonese Cuisine Emperor  
For lunch, head to **Cantonese Cuisine Emperor**, a Western-style restaurant offering a mix of flavors. Enjoy a relaxed meal in a modern setting.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Western  
- **Average Cost**: ¥130.5  

---

### 14:00–14:30 | Big Wild Goose Pagoda North Square Music Fountain  
After lunch, visit the **Big Wild Goose Pagoda North Square Music Fountain**, one of the largest music fountains in Asia. Marvel at the synchronized water displays, laser shows, and stunning sculptures. The fountain’s eight-level cascade pool and 1024 nozzle points create mesmerizing water patterns.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 20-30 minutes  

---

### 16:00–17:30 | Daci'en Temple  
Next, explore **Daci'en Temple**, a historic Buddhist temple with deep ties to the Tang Dynasty. Admire the temple’s grandeur and learn about its role in Chinese Buddhism, including its connection to Xuanzang, the famous monk who translated Buddhist scriptures. The temple’s architecture and serene atmosphere make it a must-visit.  
- **Opening Hours**: 08:30–17:40 (Admission ends at 16:40)  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥30  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1-2 hours  

---

### 18:00–20:00 | Great Tang All Day Mall

### 10:30–12:30 | Hong Kong Palace Museum  
Begin your day at the **Hong Kong Palace Museum**, where you can admire over 900 precious cultural relics from the Palace Museum, some never before publicly displayed. The museum offers a fresh perspective on Chinese culture and art, with exhibitions like "Tracing the Origins of Chinese Civilization" and "When the Forbidden City Meets the Palace of Versailles."

- **Entrance Fee**: HK$64

- **Average Cost**: HK$2,479.5

Explore **Central**, Hong Kong's bustling political and commercial hub. Wander through its mix of colonial architecture and modern skyscrapers, visit iconic landmarks like the Bank of China Tower, and shop at high-end malls like Landmark Plaza.

- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 20-30 minutes

- **Entrance Fee**: Free

**Day 1 Itinerary: Shanghai to Chengdu **

### 11:55–15:35 | Travel to Chengdu  
Start your journey with a **flight** on **SK8673** from Shanghai to Chengdu. Depart at 11:55 and arrive at 15:35, ensuring a punctual and reliable trip with an average delay of only 15 minutes.  
- **Ticket Price**: ¥1070  

---

### 15:45–16:15 | Check-in at Jiahao Yuemei Hotel  
After arriving in Chengdu, check in at the **Jiahao Yuemei Hotel**, an **Upscale hotel** with a perfect 5/5 rating. Enjoy a comfortable stay at an average price of ¥441 per night. Guests have praised the hotel for its exceptional environment, service, and overall experience.  
- **Average Price Per Night**: ¥441  
- **Product Rating**: 9.1/10  
- **Environment Rating**: 9.2/10  
- **Service Rating**: 9.1/10  

---

### 16:30–17:30 | Initial Exploration of Chengdu  
Take a leisurely stroll around the area near your hotel to get a feel for the local atmosphere. Use this time to relax after your flight and familiarize yourself with nearby amenities. 

---

### 18:00–19:00 | Dinner at Liaoji Renheju Home-cooked Dish  
Enjoy dinner at **Liaoji Renheju home-cooked dish**, a casual dining spot known for its Hot Pot cuisine. While the ratings are modest (3.5/5), it offers a convenient location close to your hotel.  
- **Price**: ¥129  
- **Rating**: 3.5/5  
- **Product Rating**: 6.9/10  
- **Environment Rating**: 6.9/10  
- **Service Rating**: 6.8/10  

---

This itinerary ensures you have a smooth transition from travel to relaxation upon arrival in Chengdu, while also allowing for some initial exploration and a convenient dinner option.

**Day 2 Itinerary**

### 09:30–12:00 | Wuhou Shrine  
Begin your day at **Wuhou Shrine**, a historic site commemorating Zhuge Liang, the Chancellor of the Shu Kingdom. Explore the shrine’s three main sections: Hui Tomb, Temple of Han Zhao Lie, and Wuhou Shrine, which houses 50 statues of Shu-Han heroes. The central axis features the main gate, Liu Bei Hall, and Zhuge Liang Hall, offering a deep dive into Three Kingdoms culture.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–18:00 (Admission ends at 17:00)  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥50  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-3 hours  

### 12:30–13:30 | Lunch at Luo Bangkok  
For lunch, head to **Luo Bangkok**, a Sichuan cuisine restaurant known for its flavorful dishes. Enjoy the vibrant ambiance and savor local specialties like spicy Sichuan dishes.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Sichuan  
- **Average Cost**: ¥136.5  

### 14:00–16:00 | Du Fu Thatched Cottage  
Next, visit **Du Fu Thatched Cottage**, the former residence of the famous Tang Dynasty poet Du Fu. Stroll through the serene gardens, admire the red-walled flower path, and explore the memorial hall to experience the cultural significance of this sacred site.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–18:00 (Tickets available until 17:00)  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥50  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-4 hours  

### 16:30–18:30 | Chengdu Taikoo Li  
Spend the late afternoon at **Chengdu Taikoo Li**, a modern shopping center blending traditional culture with contemporary commerce. Wander through its unique architecture, shop at high-end brands, and soak in the relaxed Chengdu lifestyle.  
- **Opening Hours**: 10:00–22:00  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-4 hours  

### 18:30–19:30 | Dinner at Let's Eatsy  
End your day with dinner at **Let's Eatsy**, a Western cuisine restaurant offering a chic dining experience. Enjoy a variety of international dishes in a stylish setting.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Western  
- **Average Cost**: ¥181.5

**Day 3 Itinerary**

### 08:30–12:30 | Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding  
Kick off your day at the **Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding**, a must-visit for panda lovers. This sprawling sanctuary simulates the natural habitat of giant pandas, featuring lakes, bamboo forests, and over 100 adorable pandas. Don’t miss the Sun and Moon Nurseries, where you can see newborn panda cubs. The on-site Giant Panda Museum offers postcards with panda-themed postmarks and documentaries about these national treasures.  
- **Opening Hours**: 08:00–17:30 (last entry at 16:30)  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥55  
- **Recommended Duration**: 3-5 hours  

---

### 12:30–13:30 | Lunch at Aniu Story Ecological Hotpot Mountain Villa  
For lunch, indulge in **Sichuan hotpot** at **Aniu Story Ecological Hotpot Mountain Villa**. This restaurant offers a unique dining experience with its eco-friendly ambiance and flavorful broths. Enjoy a variety of fresh ingredients, from tender meats to local vegetables, in a lively yet relaxing setting.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Hot Pot  
- **Average Cost**: ¥126  

---

### 13:30–16:00 | Jinsha Site Museum  
Next, head to the **Jinsha Site Museum**, a treasure trove of ancient artifacts from the Shang and Zhou Dynasties. Marvel at the world-famous "Sun Bird" gold foil, a symbol of Chinese cultural heritage, and explore the dense collection of ivory, gold, and jade relics. The 4D movie "Dream Back to Jinsha" is a must-watch for an immersive historical experience.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–18:00 (last entry at 17:00)  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥66  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-3 hours  

---

### 16:30–18:30 | Kuanzhaixiangzi Alleys  
Wrap up your day with a stroll through **Kuanzhaixiangzi Alleys**, a historic Qing Dynasty neighborhood. Explore the three parallel alleys—Kuanzhai, Kuanzhai, and Jingzhai—lined with traditional courtyards, tea houses, and snack stalls. Sip on Mengshan Huangya tea, try local snacks, or relax with a traditional ear-cleaning session. As night falls, the area transforms into a vibrant hub with trendy bars and a lively atmosphere.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-3 hours  

---

### 18:30–19:30 | Dinner at Xiangji Kitchen 1999  
End your day with authentic **Sichuan cuisine** at **Xiangji Kitchen 1999**. Known for its bold flavors and elegant presentation, this restaurant offers a refined dining experience. Try classic dishes like mapo tofu and kung pao chicken in a stylish, modern setting.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Sichuan Cuisine  
- **Average Cost**: ¥130.5

**Itinerary for the Last Day of the Trip**

### 07:05–22:14 | Train to Shanghai  
Start your journey back with a **train ride** on **D635/D638**, departing from Chengdu at 07:05 and arriving in Shanghai at 22:14. Enjoy the comfortable ride to your final destination.  
- **Second Class Price**: ¥606  
- **First Class Price**: ¥726

Explore the iconic **Canton Tower**, a modern architectural marvel standing tall at 600 meters. Enjoy panoramic views of the city from the observation deck, perfect for photography enthusiasts. Wrap up your evening with the spectacular **Guangzhou Chimelong International Circus**, featuring over 300 performers and 500 rare animals. The world’s largest forest live stage creates a mesmerizing backdrop for acrobatics, animal performances, and dazzling floats.

**Day 1 Itinerary: Hangzhou to Nanjing **

### 09:24–11:47 | Travel to Nanjing  
Start your journey with a **train** on **G42** from Hangzhou to Nanjing. Depart at 09:24 and arrive at 11:47, ensuring a punctual and comfortable trip.  
- **Ticket Price**: ¥117.5 (Second Class)  

---

### 12:00–13:00 | Check-in at Yishiyuan Hotel  
After arriving in Nanjing, check in at **Yishiyuan Hotel**, an **Upscale hotel** with a perfect 5/5 rating. Enjoy a comfortable stay at an average price of ¥540 per night. Guests have praised the hotel for its **excellent environment**, **high product quality**, and **great service**.  
- **Average Price Per Night**: ¥540  

---

### 14:00–16:00 | The Memorial Hall of the Victims of the Nanjing Massacre by the Japanese Invaders  
Explore **The Memorial Hall of the Victims of the Nanjing Massacre by the Japanese Invaders**, a poignant memorial dedicated to the tragic events of the Nanjing Massacre. Discover historical documents, artifacts, architecture, sculptures, films, and more, all situated at one of the original massacre sites.  
- **Opening Hours**: 08:30–17:00 (Admission ends at 16:30)  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-4 hours  

---

### 18:00–19:00 | Dinner at lingdu space  
End your day with dinner at **lingdu space**, offering other Chinese cuisine options. Enjoy a meal in a casual setting with reasonable prices.  
- **Price**: ¥103.5 per person  
- **Rating**: 3.5/5  
- **Product Rating**: 7.1/10  
- **Environment Rating**: 7.0/10  
- **Service Rating**: 7.0/10  

---

**Day 2 Itinerary**

### 10:00–13:00 | Nanjing Museum  
Begin your day at **Nanjing Museum**, one of China's top three museums and the earliest established in the country. Explore its six halls, including the History Hall, Art Hall, and Republic of China Hall, showcasing over 420,000 items, such as the Ming Gilded Bronze Tibetan-style Pagoda. The museum offers a deep dive into China's rich history and culture.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–17:00 (Admission ends at 16:00)  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free (register with valid ID for tickets)  
- **Recommended Duration**: 3-5 hours  

---

### 13:00–14:00 | Lunch at Taiyangmen Boutique Restaurant  
For lunch, head to **Taiyangmen Boutique Restaurant**, a cozy spot offering local snacks. Enjoy a variety of flavorful dishes in a relaxed atmosphere.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Snacks  
- **Average Cost**: ¥100.5  

---

### 14:00–16:00 | Nanjing Presidential Palace  
Next, visit the **Nanjing Presidential Palace**, a historic site blending traditional Jiangnan gardens with modern Western-style architecture. Explore its three visiting areas, including the Central District with its iconic gate tower and the serene Xuyuan (West Garden). The palace offers a glimpse into China's modern history.  
- **Opening Hours**: 08:30–17:00 (Tickets available until 16:00; admission ends at 16:00)  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-4 hours  

---

### 16:00–18:00 | Confucius Temple Qinhuai Scenic Area  
Spend the late afternoon at the **Confucius Temple Qinhuai Scenic Area**, a vibrant cultural hub centered around the Qinhuai River. Stroll through the ancient architecture of the Confucius Temple and enjoy a boat tour along the river, soaking in the picturesque scenery.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-4 hours  

---

### 18:00–19:00 | Dinner at Wanqing Building Food Hall  
End your day with dinner at **Wanqing Building Food Hall**, offering authentic Jiangsu and Zhejiang cuisine. Relish the rich flavors of local specialties in a charming setting.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Jiangsu and Zhejiang Cuisine  
- **Average Cost**: ¥190.5  

---

### 19:00–20:00 | Laomendong Historic District  
After dinner, take a leisurely walk through **Laomendong Historic District**, a cultural block filled with traditional dwellings, studios, and century-old shops. Experience the nostalgic charm of old Nanjing.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1-2 hours

**Day 3 Itinerary**

### 10:00–12:00 | Dr. Sun Yat-Sen's Mausoleum Scenic Spot  
Begin your day at **Dr. Sun Yat-Sen's Mausoleum Scenic Spot**, a grand mausoleum honoring the founding father of modern China. The architecture is designed in the shape of an "alarm bell," symbolizing revolution. Climb the 392 stone steps to reach the Sacrificial Hall, where you’ll find a white marble statue of Sun Yat-sen and stunning views of the surrounding area.  
- **Opening Hours**: 08:00–17:00  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥100  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-3 hours  

---

### 12:00–13:00 | Lunch at Nanjing Longgong Lobster  
For lunch, head to **Nanjing Longgong Lobster**, a local favorite for Jiangsu and Zhejiang cuisine. Enjoy fresh lobster dishes and other regional specialties in a casual setting.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Jiangsu and Zhejiang Cuisine  
- **Average Cost**: ¥175.5  

---

### 13:00–15:00 | Ming Xiaoling Mausoleum  
Next, visit the **Ming Xiaoling Mausoleum**, the tomb of Emperor Zhu Yuanzhang, the founder of the Ming Dynasty. Stroll along the 2,400-meter-long Sacred Way, lined with stone statues of animals and officials, and admire the grand architecture of the mausoleum. The site is especially beautiful during spring when plum and cherry blossoms are in full bloom.  
- **Opening Hours**: 07:00–17:30 (admission ends at 17:30)  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥65  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-4 hours  

---

### 15:00–17:00 | Xuanwu Lake Scenic Area  
Spend the afternoon at **Xuanwu Lake Scenic Area**, a serene lake surrounded by lush greenery and historical sites. Walk along the lakeside paths, rent a pedal boat, or explore the five interconnected islands, each offering unique landscapes and attractions. Don’t miss the lotus garden and the Ming City Wall section for picturesque views.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥78  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-4 hours  

---

### 18:00–19:00 | Dinner at New Century Hotel Chinese Restaurant  
End your day with a refined dinner at **New Century Hotel Chinese Restaurant**, known for its authentic Huaiyang cuisine. Relish dishes like braised pork and delicate soups in an elegant, upscale setting.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Huaiyang Cuisine  
- **Average Cost**: ¥133.5

**Day 4 Itinerary**

### 11:00–12:30 | Visit Deji Plaza  
Begin your final day in Nanjing with a visit to **Deji Plaza**, an expansive shopping center offering a mix of international brands, dining options, and entertainment. Explore the diverse offerings within this bustling hub before your departure.  
- **Opening Hours**: 10:00–22:00  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-4 hours  

### 12:30–13:30 | Lunch at 50 LAN  
Enjoy a satisfying lunch at **50 LAN**, known for its other Chinese cuisine. This restaurant offers a pleasant ambiance and decent service, making it a great spot to recharge before heading to the station.  
- **Price**: ¥105  
- **Rating**: 3.5/5  
- **Environment Rating**: 8.1/10  

### 13:30–14:30 | Visit Former Site of the National Art Museum  
Make a quick stop at the **Former Site of the National Art Museum**. As one of the representative works of new national form architecture, this historic building holds significant cultural value.  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1-2 hours  
- **Opening Hours**: TBD  

### 14:30–15:15 | Travel to Nanjing South Railway Station  
Allocate time to travel from your current location to **Nanjing South Railway Station**. Ensure you have enough time to reach the station comfortably.

### 15:36–16:08 | Train G125 to Hangzhou  
Conclude your trip with a train journey on **G125** from **Nanjing** to **Hangzhou**. Depart at 15:36 and arrive at 16:08, ensuring a smooth return home.  
- **Second-Class Ticket Price**: ¥50.0  
- **First-Class Ticket Price**: ¥80.0  

The itinerary ends upon arrival in Hangzhou.

**Day 1 Itinerary: Hangzhou to Guangzhou **

### 07:25–09:40 | Travel to Guangzhou  
Start your journey with a **flight** on **CA1719** from **Hangzhou** to **Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport**. Depart at 07:25 and arrive at 09:40, ensuring a punctual and comfortable trip.  
- **Ticket Price**: ¥500  

---

### 10:30–11:00 | Check-in at Quezhou Art Hotel  
After arriving in Guangzhou, check in at **Quezhou Art Hotel**, a **Midscale hotel** with a 4.5/5 rating. Enjoy a comfortable stay at an average price of ¥264 per night. Guests have praised the hotel for its **pleasant environment** (8.7/10) and **excellent service** (8.6/10).  
- **Average Price Per Night**: ¥264  

---

### 12:00–13:00 | Lunch at Casablanca Restaurant  
Head to **Casablanca Restaurant** for a taste of **Northwestern Cuisine**. With a price of ¥52.5 per person, this restaurant offers a casual dining experience with a 3.5/5 rating.  
- **Rating**: 3.5/5  
- **Price**: ¥52.5  

---

### 16:00–17:00 | Visit Guangdong Customs Museum  
Explore the **Guangdong Customs Museum**, a fascinating museum showcasing the development history of Chinese customs and the Maritime Silk Road. Admission is free, and the museum is open from 09:00 to 16:00 (last admission at 15:30).  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–16:00  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 0.5–1 hour  

---

### 18:00–19:00 | Dinner at Sencheng Food Shop  
End your day with a quick meal at **Sencheng Food Shop**, offering **Fast Food** at ¥58.5 per person. This spot is ideal for a casual dining experience with a 3.5/5 rating.  
- **Rating**: 3.5/5  
- **Price**: ¥58.5

**Day 2 Itinerary**

### 09:00–12:00 | Shamian  
Begin your day at **Shamian**, a historic neighborhood that was once a British and French concession. Stroll through its tree-lined streets and admire the European-style architecture, which makes it a perfect spot for photography. Key landmarks include the Catholic Church of Our Lady of Lude, the Church of Christ in Shamian, and the Customs House. The area feels like a small European town, with charming cafes, restaurants, and bars.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1-3 hours  

---

### 12:00–13:00 | Lunch at Youlian Restaurant  
Enjoy a delicious lunch at **Youlian Restaurant**, known for its authentic **Guangdong cuisine**. The restaurant offers a comfortable ambiance, perfect for a midday break.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Guangdong  
- **Average Cost**: ¥78  

---

### 13:30–15:30 | Chen Clan Ancestral Hall  
Next, visit the **Chen Clan Ancestral Hall**, a stunning example of late Qing Dynasty architecture. This ancestral hall is the largest and most well-preserved in Guangdong, featuring intricate wood carvings, stone carvings, and ceramic sculptures. The complex consists of 19 interconnected buildings, each showcasing exquisite craftsmanship.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–17:30 (last entry at 17:00)  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 0.5-2 hours  

---

### 16:00–18:00 | Shangxiajiu Pedestrian Street  
Explore **Shangxiajiu Pedestrian Street**, one of Guangzhou’s most famous commercial areas. This bustling street is lined with arcade-style buildings and offers a mix of high-end department stores, local shops, and restaurants. It’s a great place to experience the unique Lingnan business culture and shop for affordable clothing and souvenirs.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 0.5-2 hours  

---

### 18:00–19:00 | The Big Buddha Temple  
Conclude your day with a visit to **The Big Buddha Temple**, a historic temple with roots dating back to the Southern Han Dynasty. The temple features a grand Shakya Mani Hall and intricate architectural details, blending Lingnan and imperial styles. It’s a serene spot to reflect and admire the cultural heritage.  
- **Opening Hours**: 05:00–20:00  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1-2 hours  

---

### 19:00–20:00 | Dinner at Qianpai Tempura Sushi  
End your day with a delightful dinner at **Qianpai Tempura Sushi**, offering fresh and flavorful **Japanese cuisine**. The restaurant provides a modern and relaxed atmosphere, ideal for unwinding after a day of exploration.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Japanese  
- **Average Cost**: ¥93

**Day 3 Itinerary**

### 09:00–11:00 | Yuexiu Park  
Begin your day at **Yuexiu Park**, Guangzhou’s largest park, known for its lush greenery, scenic lakes, and historical landmarks. Stroll through the park’s seven hills and three artificial lakes, and don’t miss the iconic **Five Goats Statue**, a symbol of Guangzhou. The park also features cultural and recreational facilities, making it a perfect spot for relaxation and exploration.  
- **Opening Hours**: 06:00–22:00  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-4 hours  

---

### 11:00–12:00 | Yuexiu Park - Korean Courtyard  
Continue your exploration within **Yuexiu Park** by visiting the **Korean Courtyard**, a serene area showcasing traditional Korean garden art. This tranquil spot offers a glimpse into Korean culture and is ideal for a peaceful walk amidst beautifully landscaped surroundings.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–17:00  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1-2 hours  

---

### 12:00–13:00 | Lunch at Zhou hei ya  
For lunch, head to **Zhou hei ya**, a fast-food spot offering quick and flavorful meals. Enjoy their signature dishes in a casual setting, perfect for a midday break.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Fast Food  
- **Average Cost**: ¥64.5  

---

### 13:30–15:30 | Guangzhou Sun Yat-Sen Memorial Hall  
After lunch, visit the **Guangzhou Sun Yat-Sen Memorial Hall**, a grand octagonal building commemorating the revolutionary leader Sun Yat-sen. Explore the exhibition halls showcasing his life and legacy, and admire the traditional Chinese architecture. The surrounding gardens and the unique “Tree Hug Tree” are also worth a visit.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–17:30 (last admission at 16:45)  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥9  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-3 hours  

---

### 16:00–18:00 | Beijing Road Cultural Tourism Zone  
Next, explore the **Beijing Road Cultural Tourism Zone**, a bustling pedestrian street that blends modern shopping with ancient history. Walk along the cobblestone road and discover the remnants of the Song, Ming, and Qing dynasties under glass panels. The area is also great for shopping and sampling local snacks.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-3 hours  

---

### 18:00–19:00 | Dinner at Jubao Seafood Restaurant Baby Pigeon King  
For dinner, indulge in authentic **Guangdong cuisine** at **Jubao Seafood Restaurant Baby Pigeon King**. Known for its fresh seafood and signature baby pigeon dishes, this restaurant offers a lively atmosphere and a taste of local flavors.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Guangdong  
- **Average Cost**: ¥67.5  

---

### 19:30–21:00 | Pearl River Night Cruise  
End your day with a **Pearl River Night Cruise**, where you can admire Guangzhou’s stunning skyline illuminated at night. The cruise takes you past landmarks like the Canton Tower and Haixinsha Island, offering a magical view of the city’s vibrant nightscape.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–22:30  
- **Ticket Price**: ¥98  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1-2 hours

**Day 4 Itinerary**

### 09:30–18:00 | Chimelong Safari Park  
Kick off your day at **Chimelong Safari Park**, Asia’s largest wildlife park, featuring over 500 rare animal species, including the iconic giant panda. Experience thrilling white tiger performances, amusing elephant shows, and the lively Huaguoshan Theater. Take a small train through jungles and grasslands for an immersive wildlife adventure.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:30–18:00  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥300  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1 day  

### 15:00–16:00 | Lunch at Atlan Hotel-Mediterranean Parent-Child Restaurant  
Refuel with a family-friendly lunch at **Atlan Hotel-Mediterranean Parent-Child Restaurant**. Enjoy delicious pizzas in a relaxed, kid-friendly atmosphere.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Pizza  
- **Average Cost**: ¥82.5  

### 18:00–19:00 | Dinner at Redangu Restaurant  
End your day with authentic **Guangdong cuisine** at **Redangu Restaurant**. Relish flavorful local dishes in a warm and inviting setting.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Guangdong cuisine  
- **Average Cost**: ¥94.5

**Day 5 Itinerary**

### 09:00–12:00 | Guangdong Museum  
Kick off your day at **Guangdong Museum**, a treasure trove of history, art, and natural wonders. Explore its four main sections: history, nature, art, and temporary exhibitions. Highlights include the baleen whale skeleton, giant malachite, and a massive Xinyi jade specimen. The museum’s unique architecture, inspired by a treasure box, is a sight to behold.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–17:00 (Admission ends at 16:00)  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-4 hours  

---

### 12:00–13:00 | Lunch at Chang Lai Xiaoju  
Enjoy authentic **Guangdong cuisine** at **Chang Lai Xiaoju**, known for its flavorful dishes and cozy ambiance. Relish local specialties like dim sum and roasted meats in a relaxed setting.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Guangdong  
- **Average Cost**: ¥78  

---

### 14:00–16:00 | Canton Tower  
Head to **Canton Tower**, Guangzhou’s iconic landmark, standing at 600 meters tall. Take in panoramic views of the city from the observation deck, and don’t miss attractions like the Ferris wheel and Spider-Man walkway. The tower’s dazzling night view is a must-see.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:30–22:30 (Admission ends at 22:00)  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥145  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-3 hours  

---

### 16:00–16:30 | Haizhu Tram Line 1  
Hop on **Haizhu Tram Line 1** for a scenic ride through Guangzhou. This modern tram connects key areas like Wanshengwei and Guangzhou Tower, offering a unique way to explore the city.  
- **Opening Hours**: 07:30–22:00 (Admission ends at 22:00)  
- **Ticket Price**: ¥6.9  
- **Recommended Duration**: Flexible  

---

### 18:00–19:00 | Dinner at Food Market  
For dinner, indulge in **Malatang** at **Food Market**, a bustling spot where you can customize your hotpot with fresh ingredients. The lively atmosphere and affordable prices make it a local favorite.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Malatang  
- **Average Cost**: ¥66  

---

### 19:00–20:00 | Liede Bridge  
Take a stroll across **Liede Bridge**, a striking single-tower self-anchored structure. The bridge is beautifully illuminated at night, offering a serene spot for photography and city views.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 0.5-1 hour  

---

### 20:00–22:00 | Huacheng Square  
End your day at **Huacheng Square**, the vibrant heart of Guangzhou’s new central axis. Admire the illuminated fountains, artificial lakes, and surrounding landmarks like the Grand Theatre and Library. The square’s lively atmosphere and stunning night views make it a perfect finale.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-3 hours

**Itinerary for the Last Day of the Trip**

### 09:00–12:00 | Visit The Memorial Hall of the Former Site of Huangpu Military Academy  
Explore **The Memorial Hall of the Former Site of Huangpu Military Academy**, the cradle of modern Chinese military leaders. Founded by Sun Yat-sen in 1924, this historic site features Republic of China-era architecture, including the school headquarters, Sun Yat-sen's former residence, and the Eastern Expedition Martyrs' Cemetery. Guided tours are available at 10:00, 11:00, 13:00, 14:00, and 15:00.  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-4 hours  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–17:00 (Admission ends at 16:30)  

### 12:00–13:00 | Lunch at Renren Restaurant  
Enjoy a meal at **Renren Restaurant**, known for its authentic Guangdong cuisine. With a rating of 3.5/5, it offers a balanced dining experience with a focus on local flavors.  
- **Average Price**: ¥63

Head to the railway station to catch your train to Hangzhou. Ensure you arrive at least 1 hour before departure for a smooth boarding process.  

### 14:54–18:59 | Train to Hangzhou  
Conclude your trip with a **train** journey on **G1607/G1610** from **Guangzhou** to **Hangzhou**. Depart at 14:54 and arrive at 18:59, offering a comfortable and scenic ride.  
- **Ticket Price**: ¥266 (Second Class)  
- **First Class Price**: ¥421

**Day 1 Itinerary: Guangzhou to Nanjing **

### 08:45–11:00 | Travel to Nanjing  
Start your journey with a **flight** on **ZH9861** from Guangzhou to Nanjing. Depart at 08:45 and arrive at 11:00, ensuring a punctual and budget-friendly trip.  
- **Ticket Price**: ¥580  

---

### 11:30–12:00 | Check-in at Yishiyuan Hotel  
After arriving in Nanjing, check in at **Yishiyuan Hotel**, an **Upscale hotel** with a perfect 5/5 rating. Enjoy a comfortable stay at an average price of ¥540 per night. Guests have praised the hotel for its excellent **environment** and **service**.  
- **Average Price Per Night**: ¥540  

---

### 13:30–15:30 | The Site of the Great Bao'en Temple  
Explore **The Site of the Great Bao'en Temple**, a historic site featuring over 20 halls and pavilions, 118 galleries, and the magnificent Glazed Pagoda. Discover the rich history and cultural significance of this ancient complex.  
- **Opening Hours**: 08:30–19:30 (Tickets available until 19:00; admission ends at 19:00)  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥69  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-3 hours  

---

### 15:45–17:45 | Confucius Temple Qinhuai Scenic Area  
Visit the **Confucius Temple Qinhuai Scenic Area**, a national AAAA-level tourist area combining natural scenery, temples, academies, and street markets. Stroll through the scenic belt centered around the ancient architecture group of the Confucius Temple and enjoy a boat tour on the Qinhuai River.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year round, 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-4 hours  

---

### 18:00–19:00 | Dinner at Wanqing Building  
End your day with dinner at **Wanqing Building**, offering Jiangsu and Zhejiang Cuisine. Enjoy a meal priced at ¥112.5, though note that it has mixed reviews with a **3.0/5 overall rating**.  
- **Rating**: 3.0/5  
- **Price**: ¥112.5  

---

**Day 2 Itinerary**

### 10:00–12:00 | Nanjing Presidential Palace  
Begin your day at **Nanjing Presidential Palace**, a stunning architectural complex blending traditional Jiangnan gardens with modern Western-style buildings. Explore its rich history, from the Ming Dynasty to its role as the Presidential Palace in 1912. Highlights include the Central District’s grand gate tower, the serene Xuyuan (West Garden), and the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom Exhibition Hall in Dongyuan (East Garden).  
- **Opening Hours**: 08:30–17:00 (Tickets available until 16:00; admission ends at 16:00)  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-4 hours  

---

### 12:00–13:00 | Lunch at Guest appearance  
For lunch, enjoy **Japanese Cuisine** at **Guest appearance**, a cozy spot offering a variety of dishes in a relaxed atmosphere.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Japanese  
- **Average Cost**: ¥142.5  

---

### 13:00–15:00 | Dr.Sun Yat-Sen's Mausoleum Scenic Spot  
Next, visit **Dr.Sun Yat-Sen's Mausoleum Scenic Spot**, a grand mausoleum honoring the founding father of modern China. Climb the 392 steps to the Sacrificial Hall, admiring the "alarm bell" design and panoramic views. The site also features the Boai Archway, tomb passage, and surrounding commemorative buildings.  
- **Opening Hours**: 08:00–17:00  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥100  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-3 hours  

---

### 15:00–17:00 | Ming Xiaoling Mausoleum  
Conclude your historical tour at **Ming Xiaoling Mausoleum**, the tomb of Emperor Zhu Yuanzhang and Empress Ma. Stroll along the 2,400-meter Sacred Way, lined with stone statues and autumn ginkgo trees, and explore the grand Bao Ding area. The site is especially beautiful during plum and cherry blossom seasons.  
- **Opening Hours**: 07:00–17:30 (Admission ends at 17:30)  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥65  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-4 hours  

---

### 17:00–18:00 | Dinner at Nanjing Longgong Lobster  
End your day with a flavorful dinner at **Nanjing Longgong Lobster**, known for its **Jiangsu and Zhejiang Cuisine**. Relish local specialties in a vibrant setting.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Jiangsu and Zhejiang  
- **Average Cost**: ¥175.5

**Itinerary for the Last Day of the Trip**

### 10:00–13:00 | Visit Nanjing Museum  
Begin your final day with a visit to the **Nanjing Museum**, one of China's top three museums. Explore its rich collection of over 420,000 items, including treasures like the Ming Gilded Bronze Tibetan-style Pagoda featured in "National Treasures."  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–17:00 (Admission ends at 16:00)  
- **Recommended Duration**: 3-5 hours  

### 13:00–14:00 | Lunch at Metropark International Hotel Banquet Hall  
Enjoy a satisfying lunch at the **Metropark International Hotel Banquet Hall** offering Japanese cuisine. With moderate ratings for food, environment, and service, it provides a decent dining experience before your departure.  
- **Price**: ¥105  
- **Rating**: 3.5/5  

### 14:00–15:00 | Travel to Nanjing Lukou International Airport  
Allocate this hour for traveling to the airport, ensuring you reach on time considering potential traffic delays.  

### 16:05–18:30 | Flight to Guangzhou  
Conclude your trip with a flight on **ZH9682** from **Nanjing** to **Guangzhou**. Depart at 16:05 and arrive at 18:30, ensuring a smooth and timely journey back home.  
- **Ticket Price**: ¥800  
- **On-Time Performance**: 73%  
- **Average Delay**: 19 minutes

**Day 1 Itinerary: Chongqing to Lijiang **

### 09:30–11:30 | Travel to Lijiang  
Start your journey with a **flight** on **3U8679** from **Chongqing** to **Lijiang**. Depart at 09:30 and arrive at 11:30, ensuring a punctual and comfortable trip.  
- **Ticket Price**: ¥750  

---

### 12:00–13:00 | Check-in at Banyan Tree Lijiang  
After arriving in Lijiang, check in at **Banyan Tree Lijiang**, a **Luxury hotel** with a perfect 5/5 rating. Enjoy a lavish stay at an average price of ¥2034 per night. Guests have praised the hotel for its exceptional **environment**, **service**, and overall **product quality**.  
- **Average Price Per Night**: ¥2034  

---

### 15:00–17:00 | Explore Lijiang Old Town  
Begin your exploration of Lijiang by visiting the **Lijiang Old Town**. This ancient town, known for its wooden buildings, quaint streets, and serene atmosphere, offers a glimpse into the history and culture of the region. Stroll through this World Cultural Heritage site and enjoy views of Jade Dragon Snow Mountain.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-3 hours  

---

### 18:00–19:00 | Dinner at Jiuqi Restaurant Dezhuang Hotpot  
End your day with dinner at **Jiuqi Restaurant Dezhuang Hotpot**. Although it has received mixed reviews, it's a convenient option located near Lijiang Old Town. Try their hot pot specialties while enjoying the lively ambiance of the area.  
- **Price**: ¥208.5  
- **Rating**: 3.0/5  
- **Product Rating**: 6/10  
- **Environment Rating**: 6/10  
- **Service Rating**: 6/10  

---

**Day 2 Itinerary**

### 07:30–16:30 | Yulong Snow Mountain  
Begin your day at **Yulong Snow Mountain**, a sacred mountain for the Naxi people and a breathtaking natural wonder. Marvel at the 12 snow-capped peaks, glaciers, alpine meadows, and pristine forests. The main peak, Fanzi Doushui, stands at 5,596 meters and is often shrouded in mist, offering a mystical atmosphere. Don’t miss the seasonal rhododendron blooms that add vibrant colors to the landscape.  
- **Opening Hours**: 07:30–16:30  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1 day  

### 07:00–09:00 | Glacier Park  
Explore **Glacier Park**, a highlight of Yulong Snow Mountain, where you can experience glaciers and snow-capped mountains up close. This park features unique glacial landforms, including stone caves and a "Glass Palace of Lucerne" atmosphere. In summer, you can see ancient glaciers, while autumn, winter, and spring offer vast snowfields. The 4,680-meter altitude marker is a popular photo spot.  
- **Opening Hours**: 07:00–17:00 (Admission ends at 16:00)  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥140  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1-2 hours  

### 09:00–13:00 | Blue Moon Valley  
Next, visit **Blue Moon Valley**, a serene and picturesque valley at the foot of Yulong Snow Mountain. The valley is named for its crescent-shaped blue lakes, formed by glacial meltwater. On sunny days, the water glows a stunning blue, creating a tranquil atmosphere. Explore the four main lakes: Yuye, Jingtan, Blue Moon, and Tingtao.  
- **Opening Hours**: 08:00–16:00  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-4 hours  

### 12:00–13:00 | Lunch at Pullman Resort·Xi Restaurant  
For lunch, enjoy **Western Cuisine** at **Pullman Resort·Xi Restaurant**. This elegant dining spot offers a refined ambiance and a variety of international dishes. Perfect for a relaxing midday break.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Western  
- **Average Cost**: ¥283.5  

### 18:00–19:00 | Dinner at Jinquan Hotel Laojiahuotang  
End your day with a hearty **Hot Pot** dinner at **Jinquan Hotel Laojiahuotang**. This restaurant is known for its flavorful broths and fresh ingredients, served in a warm and inviting setting.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Hot Pot  
- **Average Cost**: ¥283.5

**Day 3 Itinerary**

### 10:00–14:00 | Lashi Lake  
Begin your day at **Lashi Lake**, the largest plateau lake in Lijiang and a haven for nature lovers. Surrounded by Naxi villages, this wetland reserve is perfect for bird watching, horse riding, and boating. The serene grasslands and tranquil waters make it a must-visit for those seeking peace and natural beauty.  
- **Opening Hours**: 09:00–19:00  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥29  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-4 hours  

---

### 14:00–17:00 | Lashihai Ancient Tea-Horse Route  
Next, explore the **Lashihai Ancient Tea-Horse Route**, a historic trail that once served as a vital trade route. Walk along this scenic path, surrounded by breathtaking landscapes and steeped in cultural heritage. It’s a great way to immerse yourself in the region’s history and natural charm.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: ¥30  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-3 hours  

---

### 12:00–13:00 | Lunch at Sakura House Jinqiaoyuan  
For lunch, head to **Sakura House Jinqiaoyuan**, a cozy restaurant offering authentic Yunnan and Guizhou cuisine. Enjoy flavorful local dishes in a warm and inviting atmosphere.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Yunnan and Guizhou  
- **Average Cost**: ¥204  

---

### 17:00–18:00 | Dinner at bear  
End your day with dinner at **bear**, a restaurant specializing in Yunnan and Guizhou cuisine. Relish the rich flavors of regional dishes in a relaxed setting.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Yunnan and Guizhou  
- **Average Cost**: ¥229.5

**Day 4 Itinerary**

### 10:00–12:00 | Baisha Ancient Town  
Begin your day at **Baisha Ancient Town**, the original settlement of the Naxi people and once the political, economic, and cultural center of Lijiang. This quiet, less-developed town offers a glimpse into traditional Naxi culture, with its well-preserved architecture and stunning views of Yulong Snow Mountain. Don’t miss the famous **Baisha Mural**, a 300-year-old masterpiece showcasing Dongba culture. Stroll through the streets, enjoy a cup of tea at a local shop, and soak in the relaxed, leisurely atmosphere.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1-2 hours  

---

### 12:00–13:30 | Lunch at Banyan Tree·Mingyue Restaurant  
For lunch, head to **Banyan Tree·Mingyue Restaurant**, known for its **Yunnan and Guizhou Cuisine**. Enjoy authentic local dishes in a serene and elegant setting, surrounded by lush greenery. The restaurant’s ambiance and attentive service make it a perfect spot to unwind after exploring Baisha Ancient Town.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Yunnan and Guizhou  
- **Average Cost**: ¥333 per person  

---

### 13:30–18:00 | Free Time 
Spend the afternoon at your own pace—explore more of Lijiang’s charming streets, relax at a café, visit a local market, or take in the natural beauty of the area. Whether you prefer shopping for souvenirs, enjoying cultural performances, or simply unwinding in a scenic spot, this flexible period allows you to tailor the day to your preferences. 

---

### 18:00–19:30 | Dinner at Red Wine from Southwest France Snack Bar  
End your day with a delightful dinner at **Red Wine from Southwest France Snack Bar**, offering a unique blend of **Western Cuisine**. Pair your meal with fine wines from the region, and enjoy the cozy, intimate atmosphere. The restaurant’s high ratings for product quality, environment, and service ensure a memorable dining experience.  
- **Cuisine Type**: Western  
- **Average Cost**: ¥201 per person

**Day 5 Itinerary**

### 09:00–11:00 | Explore Shuhe Ancient Town  
Begin your last day with a visit to **Shuhe Ancient Town**, a tranquil and serene destination northwest of Lijiang Old Town. Known for its slow-paced lifestyle and natural beauty, the town offers lush mountain views, ancient architecture, and well-preserved landmarks like the Grand Stone Bridge and Dajue Palace. Perfect for a peaceful morning stroll or photography.  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 1-2 hours  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  

### 12:00–13:30 | Lunch at Red Butterfly French Restaurant  
Enjoy a leisurely lunch at **Red Butterfly French Restaurant**, offering Western cuisine in a charming setting. With a rating of 3.5/5, it’s a great spot to savor a meal before your departure.  
- **Price**: ¥214.5 per person  
- **Rating**: 3.5/5  

### 14:00 | Hotel Check-Out  
Check out from your hotel and store your luggage if needed. Ensure you have all your belongings before heading to the airport.  

### 18:40–20:15 | Flight to Chongqing  
Conclude your trip with a **flight** on **8L9817** from **Lijiang** to **Chongqing**. Depart at 18:40 and arrive at 20:15, ensuring a smooth and timely journey back home.  
- **Ticket Price**: ¥650  
- **On-Time Performance**: 89%  
- **Average Delay**: 9 minutes

**Day 1 Itinerary: Nanjing to Lijiang **

### 07:30–12:40 | Travel to Lijiang  
Begin your journey with a **flight** on **MU2719** from **Nanjing** to **Lijiang**. Depart at 07:30 and arrive at 12:40, ensuring an early start to your trip.

---

### 13:00–13:30 | Check-in at Gu Dehui · Pu Shi Mei Su  
After arriving in Lijiang, check in at **Gu Dehui · Pu Shi Mei Su**, a **Luxury hotel** with a 3.5/5 rating. Enjoy a comfortable stay at an average price of ¥1248 per night. Guests have praised the hotel for its **pleasant environment** and **good service**.  
- **Average Price Per Night**: ¥1248  

---

### 14:00–16:00 | Lijiang Old Town  
Explore **Lijiang Old Town**, a UNESCO World Heritage Site with nearly 900 years of history. Wander through ancient streets, admire wooden buildings with green tiles, and enjoy the quaint atmosphere. Don’t miss the view of Jade Dragon Snow Mountain from East Street.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 2-3 hours  

---

### 16:30–17:00 | Big Waterwheel  
Visit the iconic **Big Waterwheel**, a symbol of Lijiang Old Town. This ancient irrigation tool is now a popular photo spot and a reminder of the city’s rich history.  
- **Opening Hours**: Open year-round, 24/7  
- **Entrance Fee**: Free  
- **Recommended Duration**: 30 minutes  

---
